```{r libararies, include = FALSE}
#general (from photosynthesis project, some might be unused)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(RColorBrewer)
```

```{r load data, include = FALSE}
pre_data <- read_csv("Data/TEMPEST_LeafSampleList_ISO_Ions_202605 - forR(SampleList).csv") |> 
  head(56) #kept returning 999 blank rows for some reason?
#i did cheat and manually add a plot column. seemed faster than trying to figure out the r verison
#alternative version: just delete a bunch of rows in excel
#mapping spreadsheet: its like a masterlist of metadata on stuff that can be used to do that for you

post_data_partial <- read_csv("Data/TEMPEST_LeafSampleList_ISO_Ions_202607_ForR_INCOMPLETE.csv") |> 
  head(54)


#get mean and sd for each isotope grouped by species and plot
grouped_pre_data <- pre_data |>
  group_by(Species, Plot) |>
  filter(!is.na(Br)) |> 
  mutate(
    d13C_mean = mean(d13C), 
    d15N_mean = mean(d15N),
    Br_mean = mean(Br), 
    Cl_mean = mean(Cl),
    NO3_mean = mean(NO3),
    PO4_mean = mean(PO4),
    SO4_mean = mean(SO4),
    Br_sd = sd(Br), 
    Cl_sd = sd(Cl),
    NO3_sd = sd(NO3),
    PO4_sd = sd(PO4),
    SO4_sd = sd(SO4)
  )

grouped_post_data_partial <- post_data_partial |> 
  group_by(Species, Plot) |>
  mutate(
    d13C_mean = mean(d13C), 
    d15N_mean = mean(d15N))
 

```

*Pre-Campaign*

```{r summarize ions: box plot, echo=FALSE}

####THIS IS PRE-CAMPAIGN DATA


#idea: box and whisker plots? (show range, which would be useful to know)
#can i cluster by plot but show by species? (yes! fill = does this)

#could be fun to color these fun and not with plots

#all appear mostly similar, minus a very wide range for saltwater litu
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = Br)) +
  geom_boxplot() + labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf Br", y = "Br (mg/kg dw)") +
  theme_bw()

#much higher in the saltwater plot, especially LITU! 
#control and fresh are all similar
#saltwater has a higher range, litu still is wayyyy higher
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = Cl)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf Cl", y = "Cl (mg/kg dw)") 

#not much difference across plots, it's more species-differences
#litu tends to be higher, fagr tends to be a but lower
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = NO3)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf NO3", y = "NO3 (mg/kg dw)")

#a bit of variation again, but mostly contained to litu
#beech runs mostly similar, acru is higher in freshwater and more in saltwater
#litu is similar control fresh but much higher salt
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = PO4)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf PO4", y = "PO4 (mg/kg dw)")

#nothing of note
ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, fill = Species, y = SO4)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() +  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf SO4", y = "SO4 (mg/kg dw)")
```

```{r mean + sd, echo = FALSE}
table_data <- read_csv("Data/Veg Campaign Leaf Iso Mean SD (CSV-Friendly) 202605.csv") |> 
  head(9)

# ggplot(table_data, aes(fill = Plot, y = Cl_mean, identity = Species)) +
#   geom_bar() + theme_bw()


# ggplot(table_data, aes(x = Plot, y= Cl_mean, fill = Species)) + 
#   geom_bar(stat = "identity")


long <- table_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Plot, Species),
    names_to = c("Analyte", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "^([A-Za-z0-9]+)_(mean|sd)$"
  )
 
 
ggplot(long, aes(x = Species, y = mean, fill = Analyte)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Plot) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") + #not my fave color pallette but not ugly yellow so
  labs(
    title = "Stacked Analyte Concentrations by Species",
    x = "Species",
    y = "Mean concentration",
    fill = "Analyte"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() 

```


#C, N work
```{r carbon nitrogen}

#dC13 notes: 
  #rubisco prefers to fix C12 from atmosphere
  #water stress = close stomata = stop atm exchange = using more C13 
  #so more water stress = higher C13
  #reference is a super high # so all are negative, lower magnitude = higher C13

#dN15 notes: 
  #baseline is atmospheric N15 concentration, not a sample
  #less straightforward than C13 (?) tells us about N fixation/mutualisms
  #still a little fuzzy on this

#how to graph?
  #might help to just see what it looks like with box and whisker and adjust accordingly

ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, y = d13C, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot()  + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf d13C", y = "d13C") 

ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, y = d15N, fill = Species)) + 
  geom_boxplot()  + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf d15N", y = "d15N") 

ggplot(grouped_pre_data, aes(x = Plot, y = C_N_ratio, fill = Species))+ 
  geom_boxplot()  + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Pre-Campaign 2026 Leaf C/N", y = "C/N") 



#post
ggplot(grouped_post_data_partial, aes(x = Plot, y = d13C, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot()  + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Post-Campaign 2026 Leaf d13C", y = "d13C") 

ggplot(grouped_post_data_partial, aes(x = Plot, y = d15N, fill = Species)) + 
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Post-Campaign 2026 Leaf d15N", y = "d15N") 

ggplot(grouped_post_data_partial, aes(x = Plot, y = C_N_ratio, fill = Species))+ 
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Post-Campaign 2026 Leaf C/N", y = "C/N") 



#this is an idea/proof of concept thing, not super tied to any of it
#differences
pre_post_CN_diff <- 
  merge(x = pre_data, y = post_data_partial, by = "Sapflux_ID", suffixes = c("Pre", "Post")) |> 
  filter(!is.na(d13CPre)) |> 
  mutate(
    Plot = PlotPre,
    Species = SpeciesPre,
    d13C_percent_change = ((d13CPost - d13CPre) / d13CPre) * 100, # % change = new - old / old *100
    d15N_percent_change = ((d15NPost - d15NPre) / d15NPre) * 100,
    CN_percent_change = ((C_N_ratioPost - C_N_ratioPre) / C_N_ratioPre) * 100) |> 
  select(
    Sapflux_ID, Plot, Species, 
    d13CPre, d13CPost, d15NPre, d15NPost, C_N_ratioPre, C_N_ratioPost,
    d13C_percent_change, d15N_percent_change, CN_percent_change ) |> 
  group_by(Species, Plot) |> 
  mutate(
    d13C_mean_pChange = mean(d13C_percent_change),
    d15N_mean_pChange = mean(d15N_percent_change),
    CN_mean_pChange = mean(CN_percent_change)
  )



#seemed like a possibility for looking at, but not sure how to interpret
ggplot(pre_post_CN_diff, aes(x = Plot, y = d13C_percent_change, fill = Species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign d13C % Change", y = "% Change d13C") 

ggplot(pre_post_CN_diff, aes(x = Plot, y = d15N_percent_change, fill = Species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign d15N % Change", y = "% Change d15N") 

ggplot(pre_post_CN_diff, aes(x = Plot, y = CN_percent_change, fill = Species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_bw() + 
  labs(title = "Veg Campaign C/N % Change", y = "% Change C/N")
```
